title: One Rust search-matrix config reproduces depth, strata, and leaf comparisons locally and on EC2
claim: One immutable Rust search-matrix configuration can evaluate the same ordered public roots across multiple completed depths, chance-strata counts, and named leaf-weight files on a workstation or a large x86 EC2 instance, retaining per-column values, selected actions, work, scheduling, memory, and machine analytics sufficient for exact cross-depth comparison.
mechanism: A Rust analytics binary reads a frozen root corpus and a Cartesian matrix of depths, strata, and leaf definitions, then invokes the deterministic central-frontier scheduler for every cell and writes canonical JSONL rows. A launcher packages an exact source snapshot, resolves the regional Amazon Linux x86_64 AMI through AWS's public SSM parameter, optionally creates a time-limited targeted Capacity Reservation, launches an IMDSv2-only instance with no inbound SSH requirement, enforces a wall timer and instance-initiated termination, uploads artifacts, and records the AWS and machine identifiers. The same matrix command is used locally and remotely.
falsificationCriteria: The frozen-weight Rust leaf differs bit-for-bit from the existing Rust fair leaf on any checked state, or the matrix binary changes an action/value when only output order or worker count changes.

The analytics output omits any requested root/depth/strata/leaf cell, legal sibling value, task/work/cache count, timing segment, worker utilization row, source/config hash, or machine profile reference.

The EC2 launcher can silently exceed its declared wall/memory/cost envelope, leaves an unlimited Capacity Reservation, uses a hard-coded regional AMI, requires public SSH ingress, or changes the matrix configuration between local and remote execution.
